response:
I’d block 5 findings, warn on 32, and ignore 4 for this merge.

Rubric:

- **Block merge:** high severity and `agent_risk ≥ 0.35`, indicating substantial change risk in newly introduced code.
- **Warn:** medium severity, high findings below the blocking risk threshold, or low findings with meaningful contract/operational consequences.
- **Ignore:** low-severity, low-agent-risk maintenance or asset-quality findings with no demonstrated functional impact.

## Block merge

| Finding | Severity | Agent risk | Justification |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `crime_00001` — direct clock access in `date.ts` | high | 0.44 | Eight uncontrolled clock reads create pervasive nondeterminism. This is the highest-risk finding and should be corrected while the time boundary is still new. |
| `crime_00005` — `User` contract drift | high | 0.40 | Two unchecked definitions disagree on a timestamp field. Callers can receive or construct incompatible records. |
| `crime_00006` — `Invoice` contract drift | high | 0.40 | The two contracts disagree on six identifier, money, and timestamp fields. This is a material API/data-integrity risk. |
| `crime_00007` — 204-line `generateInvoice` | high | 0.38 | A new, oversized billing function mixes enough behavior that review and subsequent edits are unsafe. It should be decomposed before becoming established architecture. |
| `crime_00012` — mixed UTC/local date methods | high | 0.36 | The same date receiver crosses time domains, producing environment-dependent results. This is a concrete correctness hazard. |

## Warn

| Finding | Severity | Agent risk | Justification |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `crime_00002` — return-shape roulette | low | 0.43 | Low severity, but unusually high agent risk: three unrelated implicit result shapes invite incorrect caller assumptions. |
| `crime_00003` — missing agent context | medium | 0.42 | The repository exposes a CLI but supplies no agent-readable commands or conventions. Add context soon, though it does not invalidate runtime behavior. |
| `crime_00004` — scattered `"enterprise"` policy literal | medium | 0.42 | Four production copies can drift; centralization is advisable before extending plan logic. |
| `crime_00008` — duplicated navigation source | medium | 0.38 | `/settings/billing` already has conflicting labels. Consolidate the source, but this is not itself a release failure. |
| `crime_00009` — route metadata drift | medium | 0.38 | Four competing names create user-facing and maintenance inconsistency. Resolve the canonical name. |
| `crime_00010` — synchronous I/O | low | 0.38 | Low declared severity but meaningful agent risk. It may block the event loop, although the actual impact depends on call frequency. |
| `crime_00011` — broad option bag | low | 0.38 | The six-field implicit contract is hard to extend safely; name the type, but it is not evidence of broken behavior. |
| `crime_00013` — negative flag maze | low | 0.36 | The current predicate is understandable, but its inversion risk is high enough to flag before further conditions are added. |
| `crime_00014` — timezone-unsafe parsing | medium | 0.35 | Two ambiguous literals can behave differently across hosts. This is correctness-sensitive and should be fixed promptly. |
| `crime_00015` — direct clock access in billing | medium | 0.34 | Seven clock reads create hidden temporal coupling, although existing test coverage reduces the calculated risk. |
| `crime_00016` — dense TODO file | medium | 0.32 | Fourteen markers make intended behavior unclear. Triage them, but comments alone do not establish a defect. |
| `crime_00017` — misleading refund-preview name | medium | 0.31 | A supposedly safe preview sends email and writes audit data. Rename or separate the effects before callers rely on purity. |
| `crime_00018` — hardcoded localhost URL | medium | 0.30 | The code will fail outside one development setup. This should normally be fixed before deployment, but the score remains below the blocking threshold. |
| `crime_00019` — hardcoded user path | medium | 0.30 | The path is nonportable across developers, CI, and deployment. Move it to configuration immediately. |
| `crime_00020` — DST-naive day arithmetic | medium | 0.30 | Adding 86,400,000 ms can produce incorrect wall-clock dates around DST boundaries. |
| `crime_00021` — tenant terminology drift | medium | 0.30 | Four aliases across routes and docs increase duplication risk. A vocabulary decision is needed, but not as a merge gate. |
| `crime_00022` — authorization rule in a comment | medium | 0.30 | The owner/support exception appears unenforced. Encode it in a guard or test; confirm whether the prose is authoritative. |
| `crime_00024` — unprefixed booleans | low | 0.29 | Minor ambiguity in state declarations. Worth cleaning up but not functionally significant. |
| `crime_00025` — one direct clock read | low | 0.28 | A localized testability issue; address when fixing the wider time boundary. |
| `crime_00026` — singular/plural type mismatch | low | 0.28 | Names contradict array shapes and can mislead readers and agents, though TypeScript still exposes the real types. |
| `crime_00027` — test with no assertions | medium | 0.27 | The test provides false confidence. Add an observable assertion or remove it. |
| `crime_00028` — manual date formatting | low | 0.26 | Hand-built date strings commonly mishandle padding and month indexing. Fold this into the date cleanup. |
| `crime_00029` — implicit host locale | low | 0.26 | Output varies by runtime locale. Warn unless host-dependent presentation is explicitly intended. |
| `crime_00030` — boolean naming drift | low | 0.26 | The negative names contribute to the flag-maze ambiguity; fix alongside `crime_00013`. |
| `crime_00031` — orphan `/account/subscription` | low | 0.26 | Confirm whether the new route is intentionally unlinked, then wire it up or remove it. |
| `crime_00032` — orphan `/team` | low | 0.26 | Same reachability concern; intent cannot be established from the scan alone. |
| `crime_00033` — orphan `/workspace/members` | low | 0.26 | Same reachability concern; retain only if an external or future entry point is documented. |
| `crime_00034` — embedded rasters in SVG | high | 0.24 | High asset-quality severity, but low agent risk and no demonstrated functional breakage. Warn rather than block. |
| `crime_00035` — broken documentation link | low | 0.24 | A concrete stale link harms onboarding and agent navigation, so it deserves a warning despite the low score. |
| `crime_00037` — 311-line billing file | medium | 0.18 | Barely exceeds the threshold and has low calculated risk. Split it when decomposing `generateInvoice`, not as an independent merge gate. |
| `crime_00039` — swallowed email error | low | 0.16 | The score is low, but this is a concrete silent-failure path. Decide whether email failure must propagate or be recorded. |
| `crime_00040` — undeclared `vitest` dependency | low | 0.16 | A clean install may fail even though only tests are affected. Declare it in the appropriate manifest. |

## Ignore for this merge

| Finding | Severity | Agent risk | Justification |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `crime_00036` — weak assertion matcher | low | 0.23 | The test has an assertion, and the scan does not show that it is actually ineffective. Improve opportunistically. |
| `crime_00038` — raster icon | low | 0.16 | This is an asset-format optimization with no demonstrated behavioral impact. |
| `crime_00041` — 254 KB hero raster | low | 0.14 | Only modestly exceeds the asset threshold; optimize through a performance budget rather than gating this PR. |
| `crime_00042` — four billing TODOs | low | 0.08 | Lowest agent-risk score, and largely overlaps the stronger large-function/file findings. Track as routine cleanup. |

The five blockers are the defensible merge gate. Several warnings—especially ambiguous date parsing, hardcoded environment values, the unenforced refund rule, and the swallowed error—should still be resolved before a production release.
